chunks: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: “al-awad” means crookedness and “al-ladad” means enmity, and this is the most eloquent expression.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between al-awad and al-ladad in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In the context of Imam Ali’s final sermon, Sharif al-Radi clarifies the nuanced semantic distinction between 'al-awad' (crookedness/deviation) and 'al-ladad' (contentiousness/dispute), highlighting the precision of his rhetoric. This lexical analysis underscores the Imam’s mastery of Arabic eloquence (fusha) as he articulates the spiritual and political deviations of his contemporaries during the critical hours before his martyrdom.
